predictions.method: 25,000 pre-tournament Monte Carlo simulations using Opta team ratings and match-level win probability model; published 2026-06-01

predictions.source_name: Academic model: Groll, Hanekov, Hvattum, Michels, Schauberger, Sukhanova, Witte, Zeileis (TU Dortmund / Innsbruck / Molde / TU Munich)
predictions.method: Hybrid random-forest machine learning combining 8 years of historical match abilities, bookmaker consensus from 24 bookmakers (margin-adjusted), plus-minus player ratings, and Transfermarkt market values; goals modeled via independent Poisson; 100,000 tournament simulations; published 2026-06-02 (R-bloggers) and 2026-06-09 (The Conversation)

predictions.source_name: EA Sports (EA Sports FC 26 in-game simulation)
predictions.method: Single full-tournament simulation of all 104 fixtures in the licensed in-game World Cup mode; EA correctly predicted the previous four World Cup winners (Spain 2010, Germany 2014, France 2018, Argentina 2022); published ~2026-06-07. No per-team probabilities published. Side predictions: Lamine Yamal top scorer, Pedri most assists

predictions.source_name: Bookmaker-implied probabilities (FanDuel and US sportsbook consensus, early June 2026)
predictions.method: Raw implied probabilities converted from outright winner odds (not normalized for overround): Spain +475, France +500, England +650, Argentina +900; Brazil ~+850 biggest non-European favorite

predictions.source_name: Silver Bulletin / Nate Silver PELE model (FiveThirtyEight-style)
predictions.method: PELE soccer power-rating model (successor incorporating SPI features) with player market values, home-field advantage and attack/defense Tilt rating; 100,000 tournament simulations; published 2026-06-10. Spain is the top-rated team in PELE; exact per-team championship percentages are subscriber-only (not retrievable). Notes prediction markets have France and Spain as co-favorites at ~16%
